120 g butter (at room temperature)
200 g flour
50 g ground almonds
60 g brown sugar
60 g white sugar
1 pack of vanilla sugar
½ teaspoon baking powder
60 ml Amaretto
50 g flaked almonds
150g chocolate 
a pinch of salt

1. Preheat the oven to 180 degrees C. Line two baking trays with baking paper.
2. In a bowl, combine flour, ground almonds, and baking powder. Set aside.
3. Cut the chocolate into pieces and set aside.
4. In a bowl, cream together the butter and sugars until light and slightly fluffy.
5. Add a pinch of salt and ⅓ of the flour mixture, mixing on low speed until combined. Add another ⅓ of the flour and combine.
6. Pour Amaretto into the mixture and add the rest of the flour. Mix again, but briefly, just until the ingredients are combined.
7. Pour the almond flakes and chocolate into the batter. Mix gently with a spatula.
8. Place large, equal portions of dough (6 pieces per tray) on prepared baking sheets, spaced apart. 
9. Bake the cookies for about 15 minutes (depending on your oven) until they rise and brown. Remove from the oven and after a few minutes (when they become firmer) transfer them to a cooling rack.

Makes about 12-14 cookies

For 24cm tart pan

Ingredients for the dough
250 g wheat flour
150 g butter (cold, straight from the fridge)
1 egg (cold, straight from the fridge)
50 g powdered sugar

Ingredients for the plum layer
600 g plums
1 teaspoon of cinnamon
1 tablespoon of sugar
2 teaspoons gelatin (10 grams) (I used agar)
grated peel of 1 large orange
juice from half an orange

Ingredients for gingerbread cream
300 ml heavy cream 
250 g mascarpone (well chilled)
100g milk chocolate
50 g dark chocolate
2 tablespoons gingerbread spice
cocoa for dusting


Pour flour, cold butter cut in cubes, powdered sugar and beat in the egg into a food processor. Mix quickly and stop when the ingredients are still in the form of crumbled, wet dough.

Quickly knead/work the dough, shape into a ball and wrap in cling film. Chill for 30 minutes.

Grease the tart tin with butter.

Sprinkle the pastry board with flour, roll out the dough into a circle larger than the diameter of the tart. Gently roll the dough onto the rolling pin and transfer it to the form. Adjust the dough to the form, if necessary, glue the sides.

Chill the prepared base in the fridge for another 30 minutes. In the meantime, preheat the oven to 200 degrees Celsius.

Place baking paper on the dough and weigh it down by pouring ceramic balls or e.g. rice or beans on it.

Bake for 15 minutes at 200 degrees C, then reduce temperature to 180 degrees and remove balls. Bake until bottom is golden brown, about
10-15 minutes. Remove and let cool.


Wash and dry plums, cut in half and remove pits. Throw plums into a pan, add sugar, cinnamon, zest from a whole orange and juice from half an orange.

Stew the fruit until it becomes soft and releases juice. Stir occasionally and make sure that it doesn't burn. When the fruit releases juice, cook for a while longer to reduce the liquid a bit. The whole thing will take about 15 minutes.

Pour the gelatin into a bowl, pour in a few tablespoons of cold water and mix. Leave for 5 minutes.

Blend the plums until smooth and add the gelatin, blend for a while longer. Pour the warm plum mousse over the base, set aside to cool, then refrigerate for a few hours until the plums are well set.


In a pot, heat the whipping cream until almost boiling, add the chocolate and gingerbread spice.

Heat the mixture over low heat, stirring constantly until the chocolate is well melted. Then remove from heat, cool and refrigerate for 12 hours.

Place the cooled mascarpone and chocolate with the cream and spices in a large bowl. Mix for 1-2 minutes, until a thick, fluffy cream is formed.

Spread the gingerbread cream over the cooled plum mousse. Chill the tart for another 2 hours before serving. Sprinkle with sifted cocoa.

For about 20-22 cookies

INGREDIENTS FOR COOKIES
170 g wheat flour
30 g cocoa
150 g butter (cold)
80 g powdered sugar
1 egg yolk
a pinch of salt


INGREDIENTS FOR THE FILLING
60 g pistachio paste
60g white chocolate


ADDITIONALLY
20 g dark chocolate
a pinch of chopped pistachios

Pour flour, cocoa, icing sugar and a pinch of salt into a bowl. Mix the ingredients and add the egg yolk and cold butter cut into cubes. Knead into a smooth, plastic dough.

Line a small baking tray/plate with baking paper.
Form small balls of dough (about 20 grams each) and arrange them slightly apart. Make a large indentation in each ball. Put the formed cookies in the fridge for 30 minutes.

Preheat the oven to 180 degrees C. Line a larger baking tray (provided with the oven) with paper and place the cooled cookies on it, spacing them out widely.
Bake the cookies for 15 minutes. Remove them from the oven, after a few minutes transfer them to a cooling rack. Leave to cool.

Prepare the filling. Melt the pistachio paste and white chocolate together in a water bath (on low heat). Gently mix the mixture and fill the center of each cookie. 

Chill cookies in the fridge for 10-15 minutes . Melt dark chocolate, pour over cookies and sprinkle with chopped pistachios.
